context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

result.summary:
REVIEWER gate on Letflow.Plugs.Admission + Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline (REQ-217) -- PASS. Read the full diff and both files in full myself rather than trusting prior agents' characterizations; independently ran compile/format/test.

1. OTP idiom: N/A for gen_statem/state-machine concerns -- this is HTTP plug wiring, not a state-machine module, so question 1 of my brief (GenServer-doing-a-state-machine's-job crutch check) does not apply here. The crash-safety mechanism (dual conn.assigns + process-dictionary storage, Mechanism A via register_before_send/2, Mechanism B via `use Plug.ErrorHandler`/handle_errors/2) matches this codebase's own established pdict convention exactly: Letflow.Engine.Wasm.HostApi's @staged_writes_pdict_key/@fail_signal_pdict_key and Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform's @staged_writes_pdict_key already establish the `{ModuleName, :purpose_atom}` key-shape and Process.put/Process.get/Process.delete usage pattern this module cites and follows verbatim. `use Plug.ErrorHandler` is the standard Plug.Router/Plug.Builder-documented mechanism for exactly this need (catching a raise in a pre-dispatch plug that register_before_send/2 cannot reach) -- not a home-rolled crutch, and no cleaner idiomatic alternative exists for this specific problem (a raise before Plug.Router's own dispatch wrapping begins). handle_errors/2 is pure cleanup plumbing (drains pdict, returns conn unchanged, Plug.ErrorHandler's generated call/2 still re-raises afterward) -- it does not turn into a second response-shaping path alongside Letflow.Api.Response, so it does not compete with or duplicate REQ-066's existing response-helper convention.

2. Supervision: not applicable/no regression. This diff adds no new process, no spawn, no Task.Supervisor, and touches no supervision tree file (lib/letflow/application.ex shows zero diff lines). Letflow.InstanceSupervisor and per-instance isolation are untouched and unaffected -- this requirement operates entirely inside the existing, already-supervised Bandit/Plug.Router request-handling path.

3. Type-safety gaps: none rising to a filable issue. pool_selector, assign_key, and rejection_detail are derived through a private resolve/2 clause-matched function returning a fixed 3-tuple shape per pool; admission_ref() (Letflow.Admission's own type, not redefined here) flows through conn.assigns and the pdict list untouched. No stringly-typed or map-shaped state introduced. Not filing a type-safety issue for this diff.

4. Scope creep: none found. `git diff main..HEAD --stat` shows exactly the expected files: lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex (new), lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex (edited -- 88 lines, all REQ-216/REQ-217-scoped plug-chain and moduledoc changes), lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md, test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs, test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs, test/support/admission_test_helpers.ex, docs/requirements.yaml, docs/status/*, and this run's own handoffs/registry.json entries. Confirmed via a separate stat scoped specifically to lib/letflow/admission.ex (REQ-216's already-merged core semaphore module) that it shows ZERO diff lines -- REQ-216's core logic is genuinely untouched, matching the requirement's own 'NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic' line. No new abstraction/behaviour/macro introduced ahead of need: Letflow.Plugs.Admission is one parameterized @behaviour Plug module mounted twice with a :pool opt, exactly matching the design doc's section 1 ('one parameterized module, mounted twice') rather than two separate near-duplicate plug modules or a premature generic-gate-behaviour abstraction.

5. Decision-record consistency: no conflict found. Checked docs/migration/decisions/ -- no entry governs process-dictionary usage or Plug.ErrorHandler, and this diff does not touch the web-framework (0001), OIDC (0002), or Ecto-schema-strategy (0003) decisions it could plausibly brush against. Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2 (REQ-066, existing) is reused, not reimplemented, and Retry-After is set on the conn by the caller first, matching Response.rate_limited/2's own documented convention -- consistent with REQ-066's design, not diverging from it.

6. Design-vs-code faithfulness: verified the implementation matches the validated design doc (including its section 10 rework) point for point: two mounts of the same module with :pool opts (design section 1, section 7's exact chain), the :release_global_admission plug positioned between AuthPipeline and the pool: :tenant mount (design section 10.1), retry_after_seconds/0 reading Application.get_env fresh on every call rather than caching (design section 4), and the moduledoc's disclosed-limitation and Mechanism A/B language matching the design doc's own wording closely enough that a future maintainer reading only the code moduledoc gets the same picture as the design doc.

Independent verification commands, run by me, foreground, real output:
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -> 'Compiling 184 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app'. Zero warnings, zero errors.
- `mix format --check-formatted` -> clean exit, no output (all files already formatted).
- `mix test test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/` -> 'Finished in 20.8 seconds' / 'Result: 113 passed', 0 failures.

No anti-patterns.md entries apply to this diff. No new type-safety issue filed (none found warranting one). Routing to TEST-DESIGNER per WF-02's step sequence -- note for TEST-DESIGNER: step-05's SECURITY-REVIEWER handoff already confirmed AC3/AC4's minimum-cap arithmetic was re-derived to global_cap==1 (per design doc section 10.4's flag) and two new proof tests were added in the step-04 fix; TEST-DESIGNER's job is to verify full coverage against ALL of REQ-217's acceptance criteria (the disclosed-limitation moduledoc statement, both gates' halt-and-respond behavior, Retry-After header value and configurability, and both crash-safety mechanisms) rather than re-deriving arithmetic already settled.
